$comment: The mutation-arm registry. Every `@:killer('<name>')` in the test tree
resolves to a `name` below or the build stops; every arm below is named by
at least one `@:killer` or the build stops; and every `type`/`method` below
has to still exist or the build stops. Run one with
`tools/mutation-arm.sh <NAME>`, all of them with `--all`.
An arm cuts exactly one way. `force` inserts `return <force>;` directly
after the member's signature, leaving the rest of the body behind as dead
code — the shape S94 measured 22 of. `find`/`replace` splices text inside
the member instead, for a cut a constant cannot express; both are
`hxq patch --select '<kind>:<method>'` payloads, so an arm survives every
edit that does not rename its member, which a stored line number does not.
`find` and `replace` are each ONE string or a LIST of them, of equal
length — N pairs applied in a single `hxq patch` payload, which alternates
old / new sections. Every pair is located against the ORIGINAL member text,
so the list is order-independent and a pair may not be written against
another pair's output. Reach for it when the cut is two disjoint edits: one
pair would have to widen its fragment until it bridges them, and a cut that
MOVES a statement cannot be written as one pair at all.
`kind` is the projected node the selector addresses and defaults to
`FnMember`. A grammar DECLARATION has no method to cut — its `@:re`
terminal is a module-level `MetaCall` — so such an arm spells its kind and
is answered by the parser (`unit.MutationArmAddressTest`) rather than by
the typer. Only `find`/`replace` can carry one: a forced `return` is
spliced after a function signature.

arms.note: a chain carrying a `#if`-guarded statement is added to anyway, so a position this rule writes joins a chain whose every resolution answers the union of two build configurations

arms.name: M-HOIST-SHORT-CHAIN
arms.note: a governed module whose chain is knowingly SHORT is judged anyway, so the statement is added against bindings the engine never saw

arms.name: M-HOIST-MIN-MODULES
arms.note: a directory with too few modules for a share to mean anything is weighed anyway, so one module of two carries the whole verdict

arms.name: M-HOIST-SITE-ORDER
arms.note: the narrowest position is weighed first, so a statement lands in a nested source AND in its parent and the nested copy repeats what the parent already puts in force

arms.name: M-AMBIENT-CHAIN-STALE
arms.note: the memo of a directory chain and of the import maps keyed by path survives a pass that rewrote an ambient source, so every later pass of one --fix run resolves against the tree that was while the plugin behind the decorator reads disk fresh

arms.name: M-IMPORT-LEAF-ONLY-NAMES
arms.note: an import statement is read as binding its LEAF name alone, so a statement naming a module stops carrying the siblings that module declares and both import rules decide a name they never look at

arms.name: M-ORACLE-FIRST-CONFIGURATION-IS-ENOUGH
arms.find: final asked: Array<OracleConfig> = cut < 0 ? oracles : oracles.slice(0, cut + 1);
arms.note: only the FIRST configuration is ever asked, so an edit that compiles under one set of defines and breaks another is applied - the cross-configuration hole the list exists to close

arms.name: M-ORACLE-RED-BASELINE-STOPS-THE-PHASE
arms.note: any configuration red before the run stops the whole phase again, so one broken target leaves every risky fix report-only - including in files that target never reads and a green configuration verifies

arms.name: M-ORACLE-COVERAGE-PAIRED-BY-INDEX
arms.replace: return [for (i in 0...oracles.length) i < memo.probes.length ? memo.probes[i].coverage : probedFor(memo, oracles[i])];
arms.note: a seeded probe is handed to whichever configuration sits at its position, so a phase judging a different subset reads another build's compiled set and verifies an edit the judging build never compiles

arms.name: M-ORACLE-UNKNOWN-COVERAGE-STOPS-THE-PHASE
arms.note: one configuration whose compiled set is unknown stops the whole phase again, so its known siblings judge nothing - the policy a red baseline no longer follows

arms.name: M-ORACLE-EXCLUSIONS-UNNAMED
arms.note: the driver stops naming excluded configurations, so a net or phase shrunk to the green subset reads as covering every build

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-ORACLE-DROPS-DEFINES
arms.note: the display server is warmed and queried without its configuration's defines, so it names types for a build nobody judges

arms.name: M-ORACLE-UNKNOWN-COVERAGE-NO-VETO
arms.note: a configuration whose compiled set is unknown is dropped from the post-edit typecheck, so an edit that compiles on the covering build and breaks the unknown one is applied although its green baseline makes the rejection attributable

arms.name: M-ORACLE-EXCLUSIONS-KEYED-BY-SENTENCE
arms.note: exclusions are deduped by sentence, so a red build whose error line moved after a safe fix is named twice with two reasons

arms.name: M-GENERATE-NEVER-STALE-BY-INPUT
arms.find: for (input in inputs) if (hashIn(recordedInputs, input) != hashOf(input, memo)) return '$input changed';
arms.note: a changed generateInputs file no longer makes the recorded generation stale, so an hxml generated from an older project.xml keeps answering for a build that no longer exists

arms.name: M-GENERATE-NEVER-STALE-BY-COMMAND
arms.find: if (record.command != group.generate.command) return 'its generate command changed';
arms.note: a changed generate command no longer regenerates, so an entry whose recipe was edited keeps the hxml the old recipe wrote

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TRUSTS-A-MISSING-HXML
find: for (hxml in group.hxmls) if (!sys.FileSystem.exists(hxml)) return '$hxml is missing';
for (hxml in group.hxmls) if (hashIn(recordedOutputs, hxml) != hashOf(hxml, memo)) return '$hxml changed since it was generated';
arms.note: an hxml deleted or edited after its generation was recorded is read as current, so the configuration compiles a missing or hand-edited file

arms.name: M-GENERATE-FAILURE-USES-THE-STALE-HXML
arms.note: a failed generate command no longer makes its configuration unavailable, so the hxml an earlier generation left behind silently answers for the build

arms.name: M-SPAWN-RUN-IGNORES-CWD
arms.note: a single haxe spawn runs in the process cwd whatever the configuration's dir says, so a relative -cp resolves against the wrong tree and the typecheck and every probe answer about a different project

arms.name: M-SPAWN-RUNALL-IGNORES-CWD
arms.find: const opts = { cwd: j.cwd == null ? undefined : j.cwd,
arms.note: the parallel driver spawns every job in its own cwd rather than the job's, so overlapped typechecks and coverage probes of a configuration with a dir answer about a different tree

arms.name: M-DRIVER-CANCELS-EARLIER-JOBS
arms.find: for (let k = i + 1; k < jobs.length; k++)
arms.note: a failing job also kills the jobs declared BEFORE it, so the overlapped verdict is the first failure to finish rather than the first in declared order

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-IGNORES-DIR
arms.note: the verdict fingerprint resolves the hxml's classpath against the process cwd, so an edit under the configuration's dir leaves a stored verdict matching

arms.name: M-DISPLAY-IGNORES-DIR
arms.note: the display server is warmed and queried from the process cwd, so a configuration with a dir never warms and the oracle-assisted phase is skipped

arms.name: M-GENERATE-HASHES-INPUTS-AFTER-THE-RUN
arms.note: the explicit inputs are hashed after the command instead of before, so an edit landing during a generation is recorded beside an hxml built from the old content and never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RECORD-OUTLIVES-THE-RUN
arms.note: the previous generation's record survives while a stale command runs, so a generation killed half way leaves a partial tree that reads as current forever

arms.name: M-GENERATE-DIRECTORY-INPUT-CONSTANT
arms.note: a directory input hashes to one constant, so a file added or edited under it never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-FIRST-ENTRY-INPUTS
arms.find: held.inputs = mine == null || theirs == null ? null : theirs.concat([for (input in mine) if (!theirs.contains(input)) input]);
arms.note: entries sharing one command keep only the first entry's inputs, so a change to an input only a later entry declares never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-LOCK-IGNORED
arms.note: every lock holder reads as dead, so a live run's exclusive hold is taken over and its tree regenerated under it

arms.name: M-GENERATE-LOCK-NEVER-RECOVERED
arms.note: a lock left by a dead run is waited for as if its owner lived, so one crashed run makes every later one unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-EMPTY-INPUTS-NEVER
arms.note: an empty generateInputs list is kept, so the entry never regenerates while an absent list regenerates every run

arms.name: M-GENERATE-MISSING-INPUT-SILENT
arms.find: drops.push('compilerOracle[$index] "generateInputs" names $input, which does not exist — kept, it counts once created');
arms.note: a generateInputs path that does not exist is accepted silently, so a typo makes that input a constant nobody hears about

arms.name: M-DRIVER-NEVER-STOPS
arms.note: a failing job no longer ends the later ones, so a rejection waits for and pays every compile declared after it

arms.name: M-DRIVER-KILLS-ONLY-THE-SHELL
arms.note: a kill reaches only the shell, so a build tool it started keeps writing into the generated tree after its job was cancelled

arms.name: M-DRIVER-NO-TIMEOUT
arms.find: if (j.timeout > 0) c.timer = setTimeout(() => { c.timedOut = true; kill(c); }, j.timeout);
arms.note: a job's timeout is ignored, so a hung generate command blocks the run forever

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-STORES-A-MOVED-FINGERPRINT
arms.find: if (OracleCache.fingerprint(hxml, cwd, defines, memo) != fingerprint) return false;
arms.note: a verdict is filed under the pre-compile fingerprint even when the tree moved during the compile, so a verdict about a half-regenerated tree is handed to the next run of the complete one

arms.name: M-GENERATE-IGNORES-LIBRARY-STATE
arms.note: the library state the generated hxml names is not an input, so a haxelib version or dev-path switch leaves an hxml naming the old library paths current

arms.name: M-GENERATE-READERS-EXCLUDE-EACH-OTHER
arms.note: every run takes every generation exclusively, so one agent's long --fix run blocks every other lint over a tree nobody regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-WRITER-IGNORES-READERS
arms.note: a regeneration no longer waits for the runs still compiling the old tree, so its rm -rf lands under their typecheck

arms.name: M-GENERATE-OWNERLESS-ABANDONED-AT-ONCE
arms.note: a writer caught between its mkdir and its owner write is taken over at once, so two runs both hold the lock

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TAKEOVER-UNVERIFIED
arms.find: final same: Bool = current != null && current.identity == stale.identity;
arms.note: a run that judged an owner dead too late removes the fresh writer that replaced it, so two runs both win the takeover

arms.name: M-GENERATE-PID-ALONE
arms.note: a lock owner is judged by its pid alone, so a pid the system reused keeps a dead run's lock for hours

arms.name: M-DRIVER-SIGNAL-ORPHANS
arms.find: for (const s of ['SIGINT', 'SIGTERM', 'SIGHUP']) process.on(s, () => { killAll(); drop(); process.exit(1); });
arms.note: a signalled driver exits without its detached job groups, so Ctrl-C leaves a build tool writing into dist/oracle

arms.name: M-GENERATE-REPO-DIR-FROM-NAME
arms.note: a dev install is not traced to the repository directory whose .dev points at it, so haxelib dev on a library whose json name differs from its directory never regenerates

arms.name: M-GENERATE-IMPLICIT-HASHED-AFTER-THE-RUN
arms.note: implicit inputs are hashed only after the command, so a library switched while it ran is recorded as the state the hxml was built against

arms.name: M-GENERATE-HASH-MEMO-UNUSED
arms.note: every generation naming a path reads and hashes it again, so a large shared input such as fonts/ is read once per build per run

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TEMPLATES-UNTRACKED
arms.note: a library's code templates are not inputs, so a changed lime ApplicationMain template leaves the generated sources stale

arms.name: M-ORACLE-CACHE-MEMO-UNREAD
arms.note: the fingerprint memo is never read, so every configuration re-reads and re-hashes the whole source tree before and after the compiles

arms.name: M-GENERATE-PRODUCED-INCLUDE-IS-INPUT
arms.note: an hxml the generation writes and includes is compared across the run as if it were an input, so every generation that rewrites it goes unrecorded and regenerates forever (lime's iOS Build.hxml)

arms.name: M-GENERATE-SHARED-HELD-INTO-PHASE-TWO
arms.note: a run keeps its shared holds while it waits for exclusive ones, so two runs that each find two generations stale wait for each other until the deadline and each loses a configuration

arms.name: M-GENERATE-CLAIM-NEVER-CLEARED
arms.note: a takeover claim left by a run that died mid-takeover is never cleared, so every later run waits on a writer nobody can take over

arms.name: M-GENERATE-TAKEOVER-LEAVES-THE-JOB
arms.note: a takeover removes the dead run's writer while its generate job still runs, so that build tool writes on into a tree the next generation owns

arms.name: M-GENERATE-FORMAT-UNCHECKED
arms.find: if (record.format != FORMAT_TAG) return 'its generation was recorded by an older engine';
arms.note: a record written under an older scheme is trusted, so records whose implicit inputs an older engine derived differently keep answering as current

arms.name: M-GENERATE-PRODUCED-BY-ROOT
arms.note: any include under a wider tree than the hxml's own output directory counts as produced, so an edited project hxml the generated one includes goes unnoticed during a generation

arms.name: M-DRIVER-OUTLIVES-ITS-PARENT
arms.find: setInterval(() => { if (process.ppid !== parent) { killAll(); drop(); process.exit(1); } }, 500).unref();
arms.note: a driver whose apq was SIGKILLed keeps its jobs running, so the next run regenerates concurrently with an orphaned build tool

arms.name: M-GENERATE-SHARE-WITHOUT-REJUDGE
arms.note: a group judged current before another run wiped it is shared for the compile without being judged again, so a half-written tree is typechecked and vetoes an edit falsely

arms.name: M-GENERATE-REJUDGE-UNBOUNDED
arms.find: refuse(run, group, 'it went stale again $attempts time(s) while this run waited — another run keeps moving it');
arms.note: a group still stale after the bounded retries is handed to the compile anyway instead of being made unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-IN-TMPDIR
arms.note: the generation record and lock live under TMPDIR, so runs with different TMPDIRs share no lock and rm -rf the same tree concurrently

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-DIR-HASHED
arms.note: a directory input that holds the generation root hashes hxq's own state, which every generation rewrites, so it never reads as current

arms.name: M-GENERATE-ORDER-BY-KEY
arms.note: waits follow the declaration key rather than the lock identity, so two runs declaring one tree under different commands can take its locks in opposite orders

arms.name: M-GENERATE-ENDJOB-PID-ONLY
arms.note: a left job with no recorded start time is killed on its pid alone, which may name an unrelated process group by now

arms.name: M-GENERATE-SHARE-JUDGES-STALENESS
arms.note: the compile hold asks whether a group is current instead of whether it moved since this run looked, so an entry with no inputs, or one whose command writes its own input, is regenerated until it is given up on

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RIVAL-COMMAND-RETRIED
arms.note: a tree another configuration regenerated with a different command is sent back through regeneration, so two configurations take it back and forth instead of one being told why it is unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RIVAL-COMMANDS-KEPT
arms.note: an hxml two different generate commands of one config claim is kept, so both commands run into one tree and one configuration is always unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-READ-ONLY-ROOT-THROWS
arms.find: return 'cannot create its generation state under ${Path.directory(Path.directory(stateDir(group)))}: ${exception.message}';
arms.note: a generation root where the state cannot be created crashes the run instead of making its configurations unavailable

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-BY-CONFIG-ROOT
arms.note: the generation state lives beside the declaring config, so two configs over one tree take two locks and delete the tree under each other

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: the generation state is keyed by the hxml as spelled, so a symlinked spelling of one tree takes a second lock

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-IN-OUTPUT-DIR
arms.note: a project marker in the hxml's own directory puts the generation state inside the tree the command may delete

arms.name: M-GENERATE-STATE-ROOT-FROM-HXML
arms.note: the project root is searched from above the hxml, so a marker the generation writes at its output root holds the state it deletes, and a top-level hxml climbs into an enclosing repository

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RIVAL-BY-SPELLING
arms.note: two spellings of one hxml under two commands are not seen as rivals, so both commands run into one tree

arms.name: M-GENERATE-EPOCH-UNOBSERVED
arms.note: another run's generation that left the record and hxml as they were goes unseen, though it rewrote the rest of the tree

arms.name: M-GENERATE-RACED-VERIFIES-FIXES
arms.note: a generation that raced an input still verifies --fix, so a build that does not match the tree can veto a sound fix

arms.name: M-ORACLE-SUMMARY-SILENT
arms.note: apq oracle ends without counting the unavailable configurations, so its exit 0 reads as every configuration confirmed

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSS-SUPER-UNPROVED
arms.note: the crossing narrowings never hold, so every init hoisted across an explicit `super(...)` is refused again - the blanket refusal that made the rule silent on openfl display classes

arms.name: M-FIAD-EARLY-READ-IGNORED
arms.note: no occurrence of the field ever counts as observable, so an early read that compares, defaults, stores or passes on the `null` no longer refuses the crossing move

arms.name: M-FIAD-EARLY-READ-CALL-ARG
arms.replace: return parent != null && (index == 0 || parent.kind == scan.shape.callKind) && scan.faultingKinds.contains(parent.kind);
arms.note: a call ARGUMENT is admitted as a null-faulting position, so a crossing init whose field is passed on as a value moves and the callee now sees `[]` where it saw `null`

arms.name: M-FIAD-EARLY-READ-SAME-FILE
arms.note: the early-read scan looks at the field's own file only, so a subclass in another file reading the early `null` in a value position no longer refuses the move

arms.name: M-FIAD-INERT-ADMITS-ALL
arms.note: every right-hand side reads as an inert collection, so a `new`, a static call, a literal holding an identifier, a bare string or a bare scalar is hoisted ahead of the base constructor

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSS-SUPER-NO-SOLE
arms.note: the crossing path no longer demands the sole write, so a field another member also writes moves across `super(...)` and a write the base constructor reaches outlives the deleted init

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSS-SUPER-CHAIN
arms.note: the fix-side chain reading admits a crossing init as a co-mover, so a refused crossing init holds back the fix of an accepted one after it

arms.name: M-FIAD-DENOTES-ALL
arms.note: every occurrence of the name is read as the field, so a same-named member of an unrelated type - a bare read or a `this.` one - blocks the move

arms.name: M-FIAD-INERT-ELEMENT-ADMITS-ALL
arms.note: every collection element reads as inert, so a literal holding a foreign static read or a call is evaluated ahead of the base constructor

arms.name: M-FIAD-CROSSING-ADMITS-SCALARS
arms.find: return collectionKinds.contains(node.kind) && node.children.foreach(c -> inertElement(c, plugin, shape));
arms.replace: return collectionKinds.contains(node.kind) ? node.children.foreach(c -> inertElement(c, plugin, shape)) : ConstantFieldScan.isConstantScalarInitializer(node, plugin) || (shape.stringLiteralKinds ?? []).contains(node.kind);
arms.note: a bare scalar or string crosses `super(...)` again, although a `null` String answers `length` on hxcpp instead of faulting

arms.name: M-FIAD-TRY-IGNORED
arms.note: a faulting read inside a `try` body counts as unobservable, although the catch turns the early `null` into working code that changes once the field is initialised

arms.name: M-FIAD-NO-ROOTS-ADMITTED
arms.note: a run whose project declared no `resolutionRoots` (a `resolutionLibs`-only scope) scans the report files alone, so a narrow `--fix` moves an init a reader in an unlinted file observes

arms.name: M-FIAD-ANY-DECLARED-TYPE
arms.note: every declared type is admitted, so an abstract whose `@:from` runs code (or whose method accepts a `null` receiver) takes a hoisted literal

arms.name: M-FIAD-PUBLIC-ADMITTED
arms.note: a public field (or one of a `@:publicFields` type) crosses `super(...)`, although code outside the project scope may read it early

arms.name: M-FIAD-TRY-BOUNDARY-CLEARED
arms.find: final childInTry: Bool = inTry || tryNode && child.kind != scan.catchKind;
arms.replace: final childInTry: Bool = !(scan.shape.functionKinds ?? []).concat(scan.shape.lambdaKinds ?? []).contains(node.kind) && (inTry || tryNode && child.kind != scan.catchKind);
arms.note: the try flag is cleared again at every function and lambda boundary, so a lambda or local function written inside a `try` and called there reads the early `null` under a catch that turns it into working code

arms.name: M-FIAD-SHADOW-IGNORED
arms.note: a core type name the file shadows - an imported, wildcard-reached or same-package user `Map` / `Array` - passes as the core type, so an abstract whose `@:from` runs code takes a hoisted literal

arms.name: M-FIAD-ROOTS-MATCH-IGNORED
arms.note: a declared `resolutionRoots` entry matching no `.hx` counts as a working root, so the crossing path admits an init over a scope that is the report alone

arms.name: M-ISVAR-SLOTS-ANY
arms.note: every accessor slot counts as storageless, so an @:isVar over a `default` / `null` slot that has storage anyway is reported

arms.name: M-ISVAR-INIT-BLIND
arms.note: a declaration initializer is ignored, so the fix strips the metadata an `= v` needs to write the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-ACCESSOR-BODY-BLIND
arms.note: accessor bodies are never read, so the fix strips the metadata from a property whose get_x / set_x, or a subclass override of one, reads or writes the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-BYPASS-BLIND
arms.note: an @:bypassAccessor construct is never read, so the fix strips the metadata from a field a bypass access still reaches

arms.name: M-ISVAR-SCOPE-REPORT-ONLY
arms.note: the storage scan reads the report set alone, so a one-file lint misses an override in a resolution-scope subclass that writes the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-REFLECTION-BLIND
arms.note: a reflective string naming the property is ignored, so the fix removes a field `Reflect.field` reads by name

arms.name: M-ISVAR-RTTI-BLIND
arms.note: an @:rtti owner is judged like any other, so the fix changes the field set its runtime type information describes

arms.name: M-ISVAR-CHAIN-UNRESOLVED-ADMITTED
arms.note: an owner whose supertype chain does not resolve is judged anyway, so an ancestor the index never read may carry what reaches the field

arms.name: M-ISVAR-OPAQUE-BLIND
arms.find: if (CondRegionScan.opaqueCondRegionMentioning(tree, entry.source, name, ctx.shape) != null) return true;
arms.note: an unparsed `#if` region spelling the name is trusted as empty, although nothing inside it projects for the scan to see

arms.name: M-ISVAR-MACRO-FIXED
arms.note: a finding on a macro-built owner is fixed without a compiler oracle, so the metadata a builder's generated access may need is removed unverified

arms.name: M-ISVAR-MACRO-NEVER-ADMITTED
arms.note: a macro-built owner's finding is declined even under a compiler oracle, so the verified path the oracle offers never removes its metadata

arms.name: M-ISVAR-NATIVE-BLIND
arms.note: target code pasted as a string is not read, so the fix strips the metadata a `__cpp__` / `Syntax.code` / `@:functionCode` access needs, and only the native build fails

arms.name: M-ISVAR-MEMBER-KEEP-BLIND
arms.find: if (retained != null && run.exists(n -> MemberKinds.META_KINDS.contains(n.kind) && n.name == retained)) return null;
arms.note: a member-level `@:keep` is ignored, so a member pinned against removal by machinery no scan models loses its storage

arms.name: M-ISVAR-EMPTY-CALL-UNFIXED
arms.note: an argument-less `@:isVar()` is reported but `fix` answers no edit and no reason for it

arms.name: M-ULB-VALUE-ITERATION-NEVER
arms.note: no iterable is proved to iterate the same values, so an unread key over an Array or List is spelled `_` instead of dropped

arms.name: M-ULB-VALUE-ITERATION-ALWAYS
arms.note: every iterable counts as proved, so an unread key over a Map is dropped although its keyValueIterator reads a removed entry back as null

arms.name: M-ULB-VALUE-ITERATION-SHADOW-BLIND
arms.find: if (stdPath == null || shadowedByNonStdType(index, nominal)) return false;
arms.note: a project type named List is taken for the std one, so its key is dropped against an iterator() it may not have

arms.name: M-ULB-WILDCARD-KEY-ADMITTED
arms.note: a key already spelled `_` is judged like any other, so `for (_ in xs)` is reported as unread and a discarded key is taken from redundant-map-iter-key

arms.name: M-ULB-OUTER-WILDCARD-BLIND
arms.note: a body read of an outer `_` is ignored, so the renamed binder captures it

arms.name: M-ULB-SHADOW-COUNTED-AS-READ
arms.note: a read of an inner shadow is left unaccounted, so a binder the body only shadows is kept as though read

arms.name: M-ULB-OUTER-BINDING-AS-SHADOW
arms.note: a read resolving to the loop binder itself counts as a shadow, so a binder read before its re-declaration is renamed

arms.name: M-ULB-INTERP-BLIND
arms.note: occurrences are never accounted for, so a `$i` interpolation read and anything else the tree hides is renamed away

arms.name: M-ULB-INTERP-LITERAL-BLIND
arms.note: an occurrence inside an interpolating literal is trusted once resolved, so a `${i}` read of a shadow no longer refuses

arms.name: M-ULB-COVERAGE-BLIND
arms.note: an occurrence no hit accounts for is trusted, so a read inside a macro reification is renamed away

arms.name: M-ULB-OPAQUE-COND-BLIND
find: if (CondRegionScan.opaqueCondRegionMentioning(body, ctx.source, name, ctx.s.shape) != null) return false;
arms.note: an unparsed `#if` region spelling the name is trusted as empty, although nothing inside it projects for the scan to see

arms.name: M-ULB-NATIVE-BLIND
arms.note: target code pasted as a string is not read, so a binder a `Syntax.code` body names is renamed and only the target build fails

arms.name: M-ULB-UNTYPED-BLIND
arms.note: an untyped subtree is trusted to resolve like typed code, so a binder it mentions is judged by the resolver alone

arms.name: M-ULB-CLOSURE-BLIND
arms.note: a closure mentioning the name is judged by the resolver alone, so a lambda whose own parameter shadows the binder lets the rename through

arms.name: M-ULB-COUNTER-CLAIM-BLIND
arms.note: a loop dead-binder-counter-loop claims is reported too, so one loop has two owners

arms.name: M-MAPITERKEY-UNPROVEN-DROPPED
arms.note: the key prefix is dropped over any iterable, so a Map loop whose body removes an entry switches to the iterator that yields its stale value

arms.name: M-ULB-REASSIGNED-LOCAL-BLIND
arms.note: a local or parameter written in its scope is trusted, so a key is dropped over it and the value loop re-reads the reassigned local

arms.name: M-ULB-IMPORT-ALIAS-BLIND
arms.note: an import alias spelling List is taken for the std List, so a key is dropped over the aliased Map

arms.name: M-ULB-IMPORT-REBIND-BLIND
arms.find: if (imported != null && imported != stdPath) return false;
arms.note: an import binding List to another module is taken for the std List

arms.name: M-ULB-PATTERN-WILDCARD-UNEXEMPT
arms.note: a `case _:` wildcard pattern counts as a read of an outer `_`, so every loop whose body switches is refused

arms.name: M-ULB-UNBOUND-WILDCARD-ADMITTED
arms.note: a `_` the resolver cannot bind (an inherited field) counts as no read, so the renamed binder captures it

arms.name: M-ULB-FIELD-NAME-AS-READ
arms.note: an object-literal field name spelling the binder counts as a read, so the binder is kept

arms.name: M-ULB-WILDCARD-KEY-VALUE-BLIND
arms.find: if (valueBinder != null && valueSpan != null) valueCandidate(ctx, body, bodySpan, valueBinder.name, valueSpan, out);
arms.note: a loop whose key is `_` is skipped whole, so its unread value binder is fixed by nobody

arms.name: M-MAPITERKEY-MESSAGE-ALWAYS-PROVEN
arms.note: every finding recommends for (v in …), including over a Map where the fix declines because the drop is unsafe

arms.name: M-PFF-MACRO-SILENT
arms.find: final decline: Null<String> = CtorFieldFold.macroFinalDecline(index, builders, owner, file, folded, oracleRelaxed);
